applicant_utility.summary: There is no standalone KAIST scholarship to apply for: you tick the KAIST scholarship box as your financial resource inside the graduate admission application, and selection happens through admission. Full tuition and national health insurance are covered for everyone on the scheme, while the monthly stipend amount for the base award is unpublished and depends on research involvement, so budget as if the stipend were variable. The named tiers are the real prize: 1,000,000 KRW per month for 4 semesters (KGPS, master's/integrated) or 300,000 KRW per month for 8 semesters (KPS, PhD/integrated), both awarded automatically to competitive admitted candidates.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-Korean nationals with a strong bachelor's (or master's for PhD) record and a valid TOEFL/IELTS/TOEIC/TEPS score who want tuition-free graduate study in Korea without a separate scholarship hunt.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your entry route: Spring (mid-Aug to early-Sep, closed for 2027), Fall Early (early-late Dec) or Fall Regular (early-late Mar); Fall 2027 dates are still TBA, so monitor the official Timeline page
Book an accepted EPT early enough that the score is still valid on the online application deadline date
Prepare degree certificates and transcripts that satisfy the start-of-course requirement

If you are ethnically Korean with foreign citizenship, start the citizenship-renunciation documentation (you and both parents) or assemble certified Grade 1-12 certificates and transcripts completed entirely outside Korea months in advance
In ApplyWeb, explicitly select the KAIST scholarship as your financial resource - omission means no automatic consideration
common_rejection_risks: Forgetting to select the KAIST scholarship option, which silently removes you from automatic consideration for KGPS/KPS
An EPT score that expires before the online application deadline, or a MyBest/ITP score KAIST does not accept
Korean-ethnicity applicants who cannot produce renunciation documents for both parents or full Grade 1-12 overseas schooling
Applying to the GDI-GTIP Track, the one department excluded from the KAIST Scholarship
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The stipend amount for the base award is unpublished and varies with research involvement and college, so housing, food, books and personal costs must be covered from the stipend, research income or personal funds; KAIST publishes a cost-of-study table for applicants to budget from.
document_audit: Transcripts and degree certificates must satisfy KAIST's 'by the start of your course' rule, not the application date
Korean-descent applicants need official renunciation documentation for the applicant AND both parents - family certificates alone are not enough
EPT score reports must be sent with institutional code 0195 / department code 99
alerts: The Fall 2027 entry dates are officially TBA - do not plan around last year's calendar
The stipend 'may vary depending on individual colleges'; the College of Engineering publishes separate stipend terms
KGPS requires department-head recommendation of 'highly competitive' applicants only, so an strong application competes for a limited tier, not a guaranteed amount
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One submission only: the ApplyWeb admission application with the KAIST scholarship option selected; scholarship and tier decisions are communicated through the admission result, with no further forms.

applicant_utility.summary: KPS is the doctoral tier of the KAIST Scholarship: apply to a Master's-Ph.D. Integrated or PhD programme, select the KAIST scholarship as your financial resource, and you are considered automatically - department heads nominate candidates with outstanding academic and research achievements and the college dean makes the final pick. The award pays 300,000 KRW per month for 8 regular semesters with full tuition, which comfortably covers Daejeon living costs but is a fraction of what the master's-tier KGPS pays monthly. Integrated students should note the money starts when the PhD phase begins, not at matriculation.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Research-strong PhD and integrated master's-PhD applicants (including those from Bangladesh and other non-Korean nationalities) who already have publications or thesis work that a department head can champion.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure a valid EPT score (TOEFL iBT 83/4.5, IELTS 6.5, TOEIC 720 or TEPS 326) that is still valid on the admission deadline
Assemble evidence of research output - publications, posters, thesis - that supports a department-head recommendation
Make sure the degree requirement is met by course start (master's for PhD entry)
Watch the Timeline page for the Fall 2027 window once TBA is replaced by dates
common_rejection_risks: Weak research profile: without demonstrable achievements the department head will not recommend you, and no recommendation means no KPS regardless of grades alone
Selecting a different financial resource (or none) in the application, which removes automatic consideration
Assuming the stipend starts in year one of an integrated programme - it begins at the start of the PhD programme
